emily_cust: Hey team — our project (acct: rw-4829) used the text-generation endpoint ~3 hours ago and our trial credit balance still shows 1000 credits even though we should have consumed ~1.2k. sample request_id: req_20260317102033_abc. Can someone check?

alex_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact curl or SDK call you used and the request_id(s)? also which SDK version?

emily_cust: Thanks. We called via the JS SDK v1.3.0:
```js
await redwood.generate({ model: 'open-7b', prompt: '...'}, { requestId: 'req_20260317102033_abc' })
```
No special headers on our side as far as I know. Multiple calls with long outputs (20k tokens total).

support-bot: Note: trial grant for acct rw-4829 issued 2026-02-28 09:15:22 UTC (1000 credits). Billing logs are retained for 90 days.

alex_support: I pulled the server logs for req_20260317102033_abc — shows generation succeeded and returned tokens. However charge_amount=0.0 in the billing event. Can you confirm whether any of your infra adds headers? also send exact timestamp range if there are other request_ids.

emily_cust: we have two more ids: req_20260317102110_def and req_20260317102500_ghi. No custom headers intentionally.

marta_billing: Hi — I see the billing events for those request_ids show a flag "test_mode": true which sets charge to 0. Historically that comes from a header X-Dry-Run or SDK dryRun param. We didn't apply any promo or manual zeroing.

emily_cust: We didn't set dry run. Is there an SDK bug? We upgraded to v1.3.0 this morning.

liam_eng: tagging in eng — quick check: there was an issue introduced in JS SDK v1.3.0 where the experimental param {dryRun: true} was accidentally set when callers include the legacy param `simulate:true`. In some wrappers that maps to X-Dry-Run. We're reproducing locally now.

liam_eng: repro steps: use sdk v1.3.0 + pass legacy simulate flag -> server receives X-Dry-Run: 1 -> billing pipeline marks event as test_mode. Example: curl -H 'X-Dry-Run: 1' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

alex_support: OK — thanks. For immediate remedy we can either: 1) apply manual credit adjustment to reflect 1.2k consumed, or 2) if you want a full refund for those calls, we can top up your trial balance. Which do you prefer? also we'll patch SDK and release v1.3.1 ASAP.

emily_cust: We'd prefer the trial reflect actual usage (deduct ~1.2k). We rely on the spending thresholds. Appreciate a manual adjustment rather than a top-up.

marta_billing: Understood — I'll create a billing action: debit 1,200 credits from trial grant and attach note: "manual reconcile for X-Dry-Run bug, reqs: req_20260317102033_abc, req_20260317102110_def, req_20260317102500_ghi". ETA: 2 business hours.

liam_eng: Fix ready: patch in PR #824 — removes default dryRun mapping and adds test coverage. Will ship v1.3.1 within 1 hour and post-mortem in eng-ml.

alex_support: Marta — please confirm when adjustment applied. emily_cust — once applied can you verify balance shows updated and ack here?

marta_billing: Adjustment applied at 1760854399. New balance:  -200 credits (trial reduced to reflect usage) wait note: the system displays remaining trial  -200? Actually ensure consistent phrasing — corrected: New trial balance = 1000 - 1200 = -200 (system represents as "overage owed" until topped up). Billing ticket #BILL-557 opened.

emily_cust: Confirmed — balance updated in console and we see the consumption reflected. Thanks for the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

liam_eng: Postmortem will include: root cause = SDK v1.3.0 simulate->dryRun mapping; action items = release v1.3.1, add server-side guard to ignore untrusted test headers from SDKs without auth scope, and add alert when billing events have unexpected test_mode=true.

alex_support: Glad that's resolved. Reopen thread if anything else. :white_check_mark:
